For all the inhabitants of the land have become melted before our face.<div eID="gen24830" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen24805"/> <div sID="gen24831"/> <div sID="gen24832" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 3<div eID="gen24832" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24833" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>And Joshua rose up very early in the morning, and he and all the children of Israel set out from Sittim, and came as far as the Jordan, and passed the night there before crossing.<div eID="gen24833" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24834" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>And it was at the end of three days, and the prefects passed through the midst of the camp,<div eID="gen24834" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24835" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>And commanded the people, saying, When you see the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, and the priests bearing it, you shall set out from your place, and go after it.<div eID="gen24835" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24836" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Nevertheless, between it and you there will be an interval of about two thousand cubits in length: do not approach it that you may know the way by which you are to go. For you have not passed by that way yesterday or the day before yesterday.<div eID="gen24836" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24837" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>Now Joshua had said to the people, Sanctify <hi type="italic">(or </hi>Prepare) yourselves: for to-morrow Jehovah will do wonders in the midst of you.<div eID="gen24837" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24838" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>And Joshua spoke to the priests, saying, Take up the ark of the covenant, and pass before the people. They accordingly bare the ark of the covenant, and walked before the people.<div eID="gen24838" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24839" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Now Jehovah had said to Joshua, To-day will I begin to magnify thee in the eyes of all Israel, that they may know that in the same way as I was with Moses will I be with thee.<div eID="gen24839" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24840" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>Thou, therefore, wilt command the priests bearing the ark of the covenant, saying, When you shall have gone in as far as the extremity (outer edge) of the water of the Jordan, you shall stand in the Jordan.<div eID="gen24840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24841" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And Joshua said to the children of Israel, Come hither, and hear the words of Jehovah your God.<div eID="gen24841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24842" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Joshua likewise said, Hereby shall you know that there is a living God in the midst of you, and that he will thoroughly drive out before you the Canaanite, the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Perizzite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Jebusite.<div eID="gen24842" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24843" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Behold the ark of the covenant of the ruler of the whole earth will pass before you through the Jordan.<div eID="gen24843" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24844" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Now, therefore, select for you twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one for each tribe.<div eID="gen24844" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24845" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>And when the soles of the feet of the priests bearing the ark of Jehovah, the ruler of the whole earth, shall have rested in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off, and the waters flowing from above shall stand in one heap.<div eID="gen24845" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24846" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>And it was that when the people set out to cross the Jordan, the priests who bore the ark of the covenant were before the people.<div eID="gen24846" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24847" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>And after those who bare the ark came even to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in the extremity of the waters, (now the Jordan was full beyond all its banks the whole time of harvest,)<div eID="gen24847" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24848" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>The waters which descended from above stood, and rose up into one heap very far, from the city Adam which is at the side of Sarthan, and those which descended to the sea of the desert, the sea of salt, were consumed, were cut off: and the people crossed over against Jericho.<div eID="gen24848" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24849" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>And the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood unencumbered <hi type="italic">(or </hi>prepared) on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed through dry ground, until the whole people made an end of passing the Jordan.<div eID="gen24849" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen24831"/> <div sID="gen24850"/> <div sID="gen24851" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 4<div eID="gen24851" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24852" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>And it was after the whole people made an end of passing the Jordan; because Jehovah had spoken to Joshua, saying,<div eID="gen24852" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24853" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Take for you from the people twelve men, one man from each tribe;<div eID="gen24853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24854" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>And command them, saying, Take for you hence out of the midst of the Jordan, from the place where the feet of the unencumbered priests stand, twelve stones which you shall carry with you, and deposit in the place where you shall remain this night.<div eID="gen24854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24855" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Then Joshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed out of the children of Israel, one from each tribe.<div eID="gen24855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24856" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>And Joshua said to them, Pass before the ark of Jehovah your God through the midst of the Jordan, and let every one of you take up among you, <hi type="italic">(Hebrew, </hi>in the midst of you,) when your children shall to-morrow ask their fathers, What are those stones beside you?<div eID="gen24857" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24858" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Then you may answer them, When the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, when, I say, it was crossing the type="bold">8 </hi>The children of Israel accordingly did as Joshua had commanded, and took up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as Jehovah had spoken to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel, and they brought them with them to the place where they passed the night, and laid them down there.<div eID="gen24859" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24860" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Joshua also erected twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan under the station of the feet of the priests who were carrying the ark of the covenant, and they have remained there even to this day.<div eID="gen24860" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24861" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>And the priests, bearing the ark, kept standing in the midst of the Jordan, till all the speech which Jehovah had commanded Joshua to speak to the people was finished; exactly as Moses had commanded Joshua himself: but the people made haste in passing.<div eID="gen24861" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24862" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>And when the whole people had made an end of passing, the ark of Jehovah passed, and the priests in presence of the people.<div eID="gen24862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24863" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>The children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh also passed over armed before the children of Israel; in like manner as Moses had spoken to them.<div eID="gen24863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24864" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Forty thousand armed men passed over in presence of Jehovah to battle to the plains of Jericho.<div eID="gen24864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24865" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>On that day Jehovah magnified Joshua in the eyes of all Israel, and they feared him just as they had feared Moses all the days of his life.<div eID="gen24865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24866" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>And Jehovah spoke unto Joshua, saying,<div eID="gen24866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24867" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Command the priests bearing the ark of the testimony to ascend from the Jordan.<div eID="gen24867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24868" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>And Joshua commanded the priests, saying, Ascend from the Jordan.<div eID="gen24868" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24869" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>Moreover, when the priests, bearing the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, had ascended from the midst of the Jordan, and the soles of the feet of the priests were transferred to the dry land, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place, and they flowed as yesterday and the day before yesterday above all its banks.<div eID="gen24869" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24870" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>Now the people ascended from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal in the east district of Jericho.<div eID="gen24870" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24871" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>And the twelve stones which they had brought out of the Jordan, Joshua placed in Gilgal.<div eID="gen24871" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24872" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>And he spoke to the children of Israel, saying, When your sons shall to-morrow ask their sons, saying, What mean those stones?<div eID="gen24872" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24873" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>You shall explain to your sons, saying, Israel passed through the dry land across that Jordan:<div eID="gen24873" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24874" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>Since Jehovah your God dried the waters of Jordan from before your face until you passed over; in like manner as Jehovah your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up from before our face till we passed over;<div eID="gen24874" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24875" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>That all the nations of the earth may recognize the hand of Jehovah, how mighty he is; that you may, during all days, fear Jehovah your God.<div eID="gen24875" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen24850"/> <div sID="gen24876"/> <div sID="gen24877" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 5<div eID="gen24877" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24878" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>And it was when all the Amorite kings who were beyond the Jordan, on the west, and all the Canaanitish kings who were near the sea, had heard that Jehovah had dried up the waters of the Jordan from before the children of Israel till they passed over, their heart was melted, and there was no longer any spirit in them before the children of Israel.<div eID="gen24878" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24879" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>At that time Jehovah said to Joshua, Make for thee sharp knives, and again circumcise the children of Israel the second time.<div eID="gen24879" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24880" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>And Joshua made himself sharp knives, and circumcised the children of Israel on the hill of foreskins.<div eID="gen24880" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24881" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Now this is the reason why Joshua circumcised them. The whole people who had come out from Egypt, all the males, men of war, had died in the desert on the way after they had come out from Egypt.<div eID="gen24881" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24882" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>For the whole people who came out had been circumcised, but the whole people who had been born in the desert on the way, after they had come out from Egypt, they had not circumcised.<div eID="gen24882" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24883" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>For the children of Israel walked through the desert till the extinction of the whole race of the men of war, who had come out from Egypt, who had not listened to the voice of Jehovah, to whom Jehovah had sworn that he would not show the land of which he had sworn to their fathers that he would give them — a land flowing with milk and honey.<div eID="gen24883" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24884" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>Their sons accordingly whom he substituted in their place, Joshua circumcised, because they were uncircumcised; for they had not circumcised them by the way.<div eID="gen24884" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24885" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>And when the whole people were circumcised, they remained in their place in the camp till they were healed.<div eID="gen24885" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24886" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>Jehovah said to Joshua, This day have I rolled off the reproach of Egypt from you. And he called the name of that place Gilgal even to this day.<div eID="gen24886" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24887" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>The children of Israel therefore encamped in Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Jericho.<div eID="gen24887" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24888" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>And they ate unfermented bread of the produce of the land, the day after the Passover, and cake on the very same day.<div eID="gen24888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24889" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>And the manna ceased the day after they ate of the corn of the country, nor had the children of Israel manna any longer, but they ate of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.<div eID="gen24889" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24890" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>And it happened when Joshua was at Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold a man stood over against him, in whose hand was a drawn sword, and Joshua went to him, and said to him, Art thou on our side? or art thou on our enemies’ side?<div eID="gen24890" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24891" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>And he said, Nay, but I am prince of the army of Jehovah: I have now come. And Joshua fell on his face to the ground, and worshipped, and said to him, What says my Lord to his servant?<div eID="gen24891" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24892" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>And the prince of the army of the Lord said to Joshua, Loose thy shoe from thy feet: for the place on which thou stands is holiness. And Joshua did so.<div eID="gen24892" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen24876"/> <div sID="gen24893"/> <div sID="gen24894" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 6<div eID="gen24894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24895" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>And Jericho was closed, and was shut up because of the children of Israel, nor could any one go out or come in.<div eID="gen24895" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24896" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>And Jehovah said to Joshua, Behold, I have delivered into thy hand Jericho, and its king, and its men of valor.<div eID="gen24896" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24897" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>You shall therefore compass the city, all the men of war, going round it once: thus shall thou do six days.<div eID="gen24897" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24898" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>Moreover, seven priests shall bear seven rams’ horns before the ark: But on the seventh day you shall compass the city seven times, and let the priests themselves sound with the trumpets.<div eID="gen24898" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24899" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>And when they shall have prolonged the sound with the ram’s horn, as soon as you shall have heard the sound of the trumpet, the whole people will shout with a great shout, and the wall of the city will fall to pieces (under itself): and the people will go up every one from his own place.<div eID="gen24899" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24900" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>Accordingly Joshua the son of Nun called the priests, and said to them, Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests take seven trumpets of rams’ horns in front of the ark of Jehovah.<div eID="gen24900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24901" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>He said also to the people, Pass over, and go round the city, and let every man armed go before the ark of the Lord.<div eID="gen24901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24902" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>And it was after Joshua spoke to the people, seven priests bore seven trumpets of rams’ horns, and passing over before the ark of Jehovah sounded with the trumpets. And the ark of the covenant of Jehovah followed them.<div eID="gen24902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24903" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And every man armed went before the priests sounding with the trumpets; and he who brought up the rear followed the ark while going and sounding with the trumpets.<div eID="gen24903" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24904" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>And Joshua had commanded the people, saying, You shall not shout, neither will you let your voice be heard, neither will a word proceed from your mouth, until the day when I shall have said to you, Shout: then shall you shout.<div eID="gen24904" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24905" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>The ark of Jehovah therefore compassed the city, going round once, and they returned to the camp; and they remained there.<div eID="gen24905" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24906" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Joshua rose again in the morning, and the priests bore the ark of Jehovah.<div eID="gen24906" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24907" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>And seven priests bearing seven trumpets of ram’s horn preceded the ark of Jehovah in going; and they sounded with the trumpets. But he that was armed preceded them, and he who brought up the rear followed the ark of Jehovah in going, and in sounding with the trumpets.<div eID="gen24907" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24908" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>They accordingly compassed the city on the second day another time, and returned to the camp; thus did they six days.<div eID="gen24908" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24909" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>But when the seventh day arrived, they rose up as soon as it was dawn, and they went round the city after the same manner seven times; only on that day they went round the city seven times.<div eID="gen24909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24910" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>And on the seventh time when the priests sounded with the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, Shout, Jehovah has delivered you the city.<div eID="gen24910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24911" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>And the city will be anathema (set apart) to Jehovah, it and whatever things are in it; only Rahab, the harlot, shall live, she and all who shall be at home with her; because she concealed the messengers whom we sent.<div eID="gen24911" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24912" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>Nevertheless, beware you of the anathema, lest perhaps you touch something of the anathema, and take away of the anathema, and make the camp of Israel anathema, and trouble it.<div eID="gen24912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24913" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19 </hi>But all the silver and gold, and the iron and brazen vessels, will be holiness to Jehovah; they will go into Jehovah’s treasury.<div eID="gen24913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24914" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20 </hi>The people accordingly shouted after they sounded with the trumpets. For when the people had heard the noise of the trumpets, they shouted with a very great shout, and the wall fell down, and the people went up, every one from his place, and they took it.<div eID="gen24914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24915" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21 </hi>And they destroyed all things which were in the city, from the man even to the woman, from the boy even to the old man, to the ox, and the sheep, and the ass, by the edge of the sword.<div eID="gen24915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24916" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22 </hi>But to the two men who had explored the land Joshua said, Go into the house of the woman, the harlot, and thence lead out her and whatever she has, as you have sworn to her.<div eID="gen24916" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24917" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23 </hi>The spies, therefore, having gone in, led out Rahab, and her father, and her mother, and her brothers, and whatever she had, and led out her whole kindred, and placed them without the camp of Israel.<div eID="gen24917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24918" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24 </hi>But they consumed the city with fire, and every thing therein; only the gold and silver, the brazen and iron vessels, they placed in the treasury of the house of Jehovah.<div eID="gen24918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24919" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25 </hi>Therefore Rahab the harlot, and the house of her father, and whatever she had, Joshua caused to live; and she dwelt in the midst of Israel even to this day, because she had concealed the messengers whom Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho.<div eID="gen24919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24920" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">26 </hi>And Joshua made an adjuration at that time, saying, Cursed before Jehovah be the man who shall rise to build that city Jericho. In his first-born shall he found it, and in his younger son shall he set up its gates.<div eID="gen24920" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24921" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27 </hi>And Jehovah was with Joshua, and his fame was in the whole land.<div eID="gen24921" type="x-p"/><div eID="gen24893"/> <div sID="gen24922"/> <div sID="gen24923" type="x-p"/>CHAPTER 7<div eID="gen24923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24924" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">1 </hi>Now the children of Israel transgressed with transgression (grievously) in the anathema, inasmuch as Achan, son of Charmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the anathema; and the wrath of Jehovah was kindled against the children of Israel.<div eID="gen24924" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24925" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">2 </hi>Moreover, Joshua sent men from Jericho against Hai, which was near Bethaven to the east of Bethel, and he spoke with them, saying, Go up and explore the land. The men accordingly went up and explored Hai.<div eID="gen24925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24926" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">3 </hi>And having returned to Joshua, they said to him, Let not the whole people go up; let about two thousand men, or about three thousand men go up, and they shall smite Hai.<div eID="gen24926" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24927" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">4 </hi>About three thousand men therefore went up from the people, and they fled before the men of Hai.<div eID="gen24927" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24928" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">5 </hi>And they smote about thirty-six men of them, and pursued them from the gate even to Sebarim, and smote them in the descent; and thus the heart of the people was melted, and was like water.<div eID="gen24928" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24929" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">6 </hi>Moreover, Joshua rent his clothes, and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of Jehovah even till evening, himself and the elders of Israel, and they put dust upon their head.<div eID="gen24929" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24930" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">7 </hi>And Joshua said, Ah, ah! Sovereign Jehovah, how is it that thou has brought this people across the Jordan, that thou might deliver us into the hand of the Amorite, who will destroy us? Would that it had pleased us to remain in the desert beyond the Jordan!<div eID="gen24930" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24931" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">8 </hi>O Lord, what shall I say after Israel turns his back before his enemies?<div eID="gen24931" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24932" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">9 </hi>And the Canaanite and all the inhabitants of the land will hear, and will turn against us, and will destroy our name from the earth; and what wilt thou do to thy great name?<div eID="gen24932" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24933" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">10 </hi>Then Jehovah said to Joshua, Arise. Why is it that thou thus falls upon thy face?<div eID="gen24933" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24934" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">11 </hi>Israel has sinned, and they have even transgressed my paction which I enjoined upon them, and they have also taken of the anathema, and they have also stolen, and they have also lied, and they have also deposited it among their vessels.<div eID="gen24934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24935" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12 </hi>Therefore the children of Israel have not been able to stand before their enemies; they will turn their back before their enemies; because they are in anathema, I will not continue to be with you, unless you destroy the anathema from the midst of you.<div eID="gen24935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24936" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13 </hi>Arise, sanctify the people, and say, Sanctify yourselves against to-morrow; for thus says Jehovah, God of Israel, there is anathema in the midst of thee, Israel.<div eID="gen24936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24937" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14 </hi>You shall therefore come near in the morning by your tribes; and the tribe which Jehovah shall detect will come near by families; and the family which Jehovah shall detect shall come near by houses; and the house which Jehovah shall detect will come near by men.<div eID="gen24937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24938" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15 </hi>And the man who shall be detected in the anathema, will be burnt with fire, himself and all things which are his, because he has transgressed the paction of Jehovah, and has done iniquity in Israel.<div eID="gen24938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24939" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16 </hi>Joshua accordingly rose early in the morning, and caused Israel to draw near by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.<div eID="gen24939" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24940" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17 </hi>Then he put in the kindreds of Judah, and took the kindred of Zera; then he put in the families of Zari by men, and the family of Zabdi was taken.<div eID="gen24940" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24941" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18 </hi>And he took his house by men, and Achan, son of Charmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zera, was taken.<div eID="gen24941" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24942" type="x-p"/><h

                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXIV.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>AND Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">To wit, by their Representatives, as <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 23. 2.</ns0:note> to Shechem <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Either 1. To <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> where the Ark and Tabernacle was; because they are here said <ns0:hi>to present themselves before God;</ns0:hi> and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause the Stone set up here is said to be <ns0:hi>set up in or by the Sanctuary of the Lord;</ns0:hi> of both which I shall speak in their proper places. And they say <ns0:hi>Shilob</ns0:hi> is here called <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> because it was in the Territory of <ns0:hi>Shechem;</ns0:hi> but that may be doubted, seeing <ns0:hi>Shiloh</ns0:hi> was Ten Miles distant from <ns0:hi>She<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chem,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>S. Ierom</ns0:hi> affirms. And had he meant <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> why should he not express it in its known and proper name, by which it is called in all other places, rather than by another name no where else given to it? Or rather, 2. To the City of <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> a place convenient for the present purpose, not only because it was a <ns0:hi>Levitical</ns0:hi> City, and a City of Refuge, and a place near to <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi>'s City, but especially for the two main ends for which he summoned them thither, 1. For the solemn Burial of the <ns0:hi>Bones of Ioseph,</ns0:hi> as is implyed here <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32. and of the rest of the Patriarchs, as is noted <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 7. 15, 16. for which this place was designed. 2. For the solemn renewing of their Covenant with God; which in this place was first made between God and <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> Gen. 12. 6, 7. and afterwards was there renewed by the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> at their first entrance into the Land of <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> between the two moun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tains of <ns0:hi>Ebal</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gerizim,</ns0:hi> Jos. 8. 30, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> which were very near <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> as appears from <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 9. 6, 7. and therefore this place was most proper, both to remind them of their former obligations to God, and to engage them to a farther ratification of them.</ns0:note>, and called for the elders of Israel, and for the heads, and for the judges, and for their officers, and they presented themselves be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Either 1. Before the Ark or Taber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nacle, as that Phrase is commonly used; which might be either in <ns0:hi>Shiloh,</ns0:hi> where they were fixed; or in <ns0:hi>Shechem,</ns0:hi> whether the Ark was brought upon this great occasion, as it was sometimes removed upon such occasions, as 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 4. 3. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 15. 24. Or 2. In that Publick, and Ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nerable, and Sacred Assembly met together for Religious Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ercises; for in such God is present, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20. 24. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 82. 1. <ns0:hi>Ma<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi> 18. 20. Or 3. As in Gods Presence, to hear what <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shua</ns0:hi> was to speak to them in Gods Name, and to receive Gods Commands from his mouth. Thus <ns0:hi>Isaac</ns0:hi> is said to <ns0:hi>Bless</ns0:hi> Jacob <ns0:hi>before the Lord,</ns0:hi> i. e. in his Name and Presence, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 27. 7. and <ns0:hi>Ieptha</ns0:hi> is said to <ns0:hi>utter all his words before the Lord in</ns0:hi> Mizpeh, i. e. as in Gods Presence, calling him in to be Witness of them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And Joshua said unto all the people <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">i. e. That people which were present, to wit, to the <ns0:hi>Elders,</ns0:hi> &c. by whom it was to be imparted to all the rest, and to as many of the people as came thither.</ns0:note>, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 11. 26, 31. and 12. 1.</ns0:note> your fathers dwelt on the other side of the floud <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>the River,</ns0:hi> to wit, <ns0:hi>Euphrates,</ns0:hi> as all agree, so called by way of Eminency.</ns0:note>

Both <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Nahor</ns0:hi> were no less Idolaters than the rest of Mankind.                   <ns0:p n="15">15 And if it seem evil <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Unjust, unreasonable or inconvenient.</ns0:note> unto you to serve the LORD, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 6. 67.</ns0:note> choose ye this day whom ye will serve <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Not that he leaves them to their liberty, whether they would serve God or Idols; for <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> had no such power or liberty him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self, nor could give it to any other; and both he and they were obliged by the Law of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> to give their Worship to God only, and to forbear all Idolatry in themselves, and severely to punish it in others; but it is a Rhetorical and powerful insinuation, whereby he both implies, That the Worship of God is so highly reasonable, so necessary and beneficial; and the service of Idols is so absurd, and vain, and pernicious, that, if it were left free to all men to make their choice, every man in his right Wits must needs chuse the Service of God, before that of Idols; and provokes them to bind themselves faster to God by their own choice.                   <ns0:p n="16">16 And the people answered and said, God for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 For the LORD our God he <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> that brought us up, and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and which did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way wherein we went, and among all the people through whom we passed.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And the LORD drave out from before us all the people, even the Amorites which dwelt in the land: <ns0:hi>therefore</ns0:hi> will we also serve the LORD, for he is our God.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And Joshua said unto the people, Ye cannot serve the LORD <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He speaks not of an absolute impossibility, (for then both his resolution to serve God himself, and his exhortati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on to them to do so, had been vain and ridiculous; but of a moral impossibility, or a very great difficulty, which he alledgeth, not to discourage them from Gods Service, which is his great design to engage them in; but only to make them more considerate and cautious in obliging themselves; and more circumspect and resolved in answering their obligati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons. The meaning is, Gods Service is not, as you seem to fancy, a slight and easy thing, as soon done as said; but it is a work of great difficulty, and requires great care, and courage and resolution; and when I consider the infinite purity of God, that he will not be mocked or abused; and withal your great and often manifested proneness to Super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stition and Idolatry, even during the Life of <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> and in some of you, whilst I live, and whilest the obligations which God hath laid upon you in this Land, are fresh in remembrance; I cannot but fear that after my Decease you will think the Service of God too hard and bur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />densom for you, and therefore will cast it off, and revolt from him, if you do not double your Watch, and carefully avoid all occasions of Idolatry, which I fear you will not do, but I do hereby exhort you to do.</ns0:note>: for he <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> an holy God: he is a jealous God <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">He will not endure a corrival, or partner in his Worship;
